title: Chronicon Paschale (Easter Chronicle; «Пасхальная хроника»). Proposed unit: the Epitome from Abraham to AD 284
author: Anonymous (cleric close to Patriarch Sergius I)
genre: Christian world chronicle / chronography with consular fasti and Olympiads
size: Whole work c. 730 Bonn pp. (Dindorf I). Proposed unit roughly 400+ Bonn pp. (Greek + Latin), est. 90–120k Greek words (rough)
edition: Dindorf, CSHB 1832, 2 vols: public domain, scanned. No modern critical edition of the pre-284 part
ru_evidence: Самуткина Л.А., «Пасхальная хроника», СПб.: Алетейя 2004 covers only the introduction and the Epitome from Adam to Terah. Kuzenkov's review (patriarchia.ru): «лишь первая, небольшая часть хроники». No Russian for Abraham–628
en_evidence: Only Whitby & Whitby, Chronicon Paschale 284–628 AD (TTH 7, Liverpool; 2nd imp. 2007). No English for Creation–284 found in en/ru Wikipedia bibliographies
other_translations: None found for the Abraham–284 portion (only the old Latin of Du Cange/Dindorf)
value: Transmits Africanus-based chronology, Olympiad and consular lists, synchronisms for Hellenistic and Roman history, and the Alexandrian Easter computus. A key witness to how Byzantium received ancient history. The bulk of a major chronicle exists in no modern language, which makes it an ideal Neoscholia flagship.
ai_feasibility: High: formulaic Koine, annalistic entries. Risks: numerals, consul names and era reckonings; check them programmatically against the fasti
pilot_unit: Olympiads c. 100–130 (Philip II to the Diadochi, including the Alexander entries) or the Republican consular-fasti block. c. 25–30 Bonn pp., est. 6–8k words
